entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (PTEN). When abundance in human cells and lipid-phosphatase activity in yeast are scored for the same variants, about half are WT-like on both and about a fifth lose both.
entries.snippet: The majority of variants were in agreement with both assays, as 51% of the classified variants were WT-like for both properties (Fig. 2A, green), while 21% exhibited loss of both activity and abundance (Fig. 2A, purple).
entries.anchor: Results, Classification of PTEN variants by abundance and activity, paragraph 1

entries.snippet: The remaining 28% of variants exhibited discrepancies between the two assays, pointing to subtler molecular phenotypes than near-complete losses of phosphatase activity through loss of intracellular abundance.

entries.proposition: The yeast activity read is insensitive to partial protein loss: activity falls only when abundance is reduced at least 5-fold, so 'activity retained' at low abundance is partly a range limit of the activity assay and a cross-system comparison (human-cell abundance, yeast activity).
entries.snippet: The variants in this panel only consistently showed reduced activity when their measured abundances were profoundly reduced, by at least 5-fold (Fig. 2B).

entries.proposition: Of 40 low-abundance variants that are ClinVar pathogenic or sit in a clinical cohort, about half lose activity too; the authors say loss-of-abundance-only pathogenicity is possible but cannot be separated from assay noise or insensitivity.
entries.snippet: Thus, it is tempting to speculate that at least some of these loss of abundance only variants are pathogenic by sole virtue of their lowered abundance despite scoring as WT-like or indeterminate in the yeast activity assay.

entries.proposition: The two read-outs are complementary: the activity assay finds abundant-but-inactive variants the abundance assay misses, and the abundance assay finds hypomorphic variants outside the activity assay's dynamic range.
entries.snippet: The yeast PTEN activity assay directly assesses catalytic activity, thus identifying a large swath of abundant but inactive variants that would be missed with the abundance assay.

entries.proposition: Partial protein loss is linked, in the authors' reading of the literature, to milder presentations (autism spectrum disorder, developmental disability) and gross activity loss to cancer and severe cases: a dose-response framing relevant to hypomorph-versus-null comparisons. It is a literature statement in the Discussion, not a result of this paper's data.
entries.snippet: Thus, each assay provides complementary experimental readouts that have together improved our ability to delineate how PTEN genotype impacts phenotype.

entries.snippet: Loss of abundance only variants also appeared to be depleted, likely due to the fact that, by definition, these variants retain at least partial activity, which may be sufficient to counteract oncogenesis in most circumstances.
